title: Protocol for data collection on the language of poor students in Malaysia☆
author: Wan Halim, Zaini, et al.

steps.title: Define study scope and sampling
steps.instruction: Specify that the study will use 2022 data from the Department of Statistics Malaysia, run under the 2022‑2024 grant, and will focus on five poverty‑affected zones (Northern – Kedah, Central – Perak, Southern – Johor, Eastern – Kelantan, Borneo – Sabah & Sarawak). Use purposive sampling of primary, secondary and pre‑university schools: each zone provides schools of the three levels, each school contributes five classes, and three poverty‑affected students are selected per class, giving a total of 270 students.

steps.title: Obtain research permission
steps.instruction: Prepare the research proposal and required documents and submit them to the Malaysia Ministry of Education and the State Education Department to request permission to conduct the study in schools.

steps.title: Negotiate and formalize school collaboration
steps.instruction: Send an official notification letter from Sultan Idris Education University (UPSI) to each school administration, hold a briefing session (online or face‑to‑face) to explain objectives and timeline, coordinate dates, times, classes and requirements, sign a Letter of Acceptance/Collaboration Agreement, and maintain a liaison officer for ongoing communication.

steps.title: Prepare and collect consent forms
steps.instruction: Draft age‑appropriate consent forms for parents/guardians explaining purpose, procedures and ethics; distribute the forms to parents via teachers; allow a few days for review, signature and return; collect all signed forms from teachers, file them securely, and verify that only students with returned consent will participate.

steps.title: Brief teachers and distribute instruments
steps.instruction: Researchers brief teachers on the data‑collection procedures and hand out the instruments for written and spoken tasks, including the Voice Memo application for audio recording.

steps.title: Collect written and spoken language data
steps.instruction: Administer the tasks to students according to the schedule: written essay task for about 1 hour 30 minutes and spoken task for about 40 minutes, using the selected theme “School Holiday”. Record spoken responses with the Voice Memo app, then collect all completed papers and audio files.

substeps.instruction: Written task: students write essays in Malay on the “School Holiday” theme for ~1 h 30 min.
Spoken task: students answer oral prompts for ~40 min; recordings captured via Voice Memo.

steps.title: Tag and organise raw data
steps.instruction: Assign a unique tag to each collected file, separating spoken recordings from written essays, and store them in an organized folder structure by zone.

steps.title: Transcribe and clean data
steps.instruction: Transcribe all spoken recordings into .txt files; save written essays as .txt files; during cleaning, correct spelling and punctuation errors in the written data.

steps.title: Code files for corpus analysis
steps.instruction: Prepare the .txt files for import into LancsBoxX (Lancaster University corpus software), ensuring oral and written data are kept in separate files for each zone.

steps.title: Validate data with language expert
steps.instruction: Appoint a qualified language expert to review the transcribed and coded files for accuracy and reliability.

steps.title: Collect socioeconomic background information
steps.instruction: Gather each student’s socioeconomic data (salary level, gender, parents’ occupations, location) to accompany the language data for later analysis.

steps.title: Conduct classroom observation (oral language)
steps.instruction: For a 40‑minute session, have an observer record teacher‑student interaction using audio equipment after the teacher randomly selects a topic; inform students of the observation, coordinate with the teacher, and later extract the recorded language for analysis.

steps.title: Administer written examination paper (written language)
steps.instruction: Provide students with open‑ended essay questions on the “School Holiday” theme (graded by difficulty per class level), instruct them to write in Malay, allocate a set response time, collect the completed papers, and store them for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Teacher selects theme and prepares questions.
Students write essays within allocated time.

description: The design of this study uses a mixed-methods approach, which includes both qualitative and quantitative methods. This design phase is divided into two, namely the Data Collection and Data Analysis Phases. This paper will focus on the Data Collection Phase that uses a quantitative design. Through the collaboration with the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), the study leverages key insights from the 2020 Report on Household Income Estimates and Poverty Incidence in Malaysia, particularly in relation to states with significant poverty concentrations. Given that the research grant was approved for the duration of two years (2022–2024), the data from DOSM for the year 2022 was chosen as the basis for this study. Generally, poverty can be measured using various methods, including absolute poverty measurement and relative poverty measurement. A household is considered to be in absolute poverty if its income is lower than the Poverty Line Income (PLI) and is insufficient to meet basic needs such as food, clothing, and housing. Extreme poverty, on the other hand, is when a household's income is lower than the food poverty line. Relative poverty, on the other hand, is a condition where a household's income is below half of the median household income. Each country has its own benchmarks for measuring poverty, but the method often used by most upper-middle-income countries, including Malaysia, is the measurement of absolute poverty. This is the main indicator in monitoring poverty eradication. This study selects five zones that represent critical poverty areas, namely; Northern Zone = Kedah, Malaysia; Central Zone = Perak, Malaysia; Southern Zone = Johor, Malaysia; Eastern Zone = Kelantan, Malaysia; BorneoZone = Sabah, Malaysia and Sarawak, Malaysia. The selection of the five zones is based on DOSM Report.
